Data Validation Everyone Can Read

Pointblank checks your tables for the problems that matter (missing values, out-of-range numbers, malformed text, duplicate rows) and **reports what it finds** in tables that analysts, engineers, and stakeholders can all read.

[Get started](./user-guide/getting-started/quickstart.md) [See the demos](./examples/) [Browse the reference](./reference/index.md)

`$`` pip install pointblank`

### A validation, one part at a time

A validation is a table, a plan of checks, and a report. Step through this one to see what each part adds, with the new lines of code highlighted.

Data

Start with a table: Polars, Pandas, a DuckDB or Spark table, a database table, or a CSV or Parquet file. [`pb.preview()`](./reference/preview.md#pointblank.preview) shows its first and last rows and its column types.

``` python
import pointblank as pb

small_table = pb.load_dataset("small_table")

pb.preview(small_table)
```

Plan

Say what good data looks like, one check per step. There are checks for values, text patterns, sets, missing values, duplicates, row counts, schemas, and more. Before the checks are run, the report shows the plan.

``` python
(
    pb.Validate(
        data=small_table,
        tbl_name="small_table",
        label="Checks on the sales data",
    )
    .col_vals_gt(columns="d", value=1000)
    .col_vals_not_null(columns="c")
    .col_vals_regex(columns="b", pattern=r"^\d-[a-z]{3}-\d{3}$")
    .col_vals_in_set(columns="f", set=["low", "mid", "high"])
    .rows_distinct()
)
```

Thresholds

Decide how much failure is too much. Thresholds set the share of failing rows that counts as a warning, an error, or a critical problem, and actions can run when one is reached.

``` python
(
    pb.Validate(
        data=small_table,
        tbl_name="small_table",
        label="Checks on the sales data",
        thresholds=pb.Thresholds(warning=0.05, error=0.10, critical=0.15),
    )
    .col_vals_gt(columns="d", value=1000)
    .col_vals_not_null(columns="c")
    .col_vals_regex(columns="b", pattern=r"^\d-[a-z]{3}-\d{3}$")
    .col_vals_in_set(columns="f", set=["low", "mid", "high"])
    .rows_distinct()
)
```

Report

Run the checks with [`interrogate()`](./reference/Validate.interrogate.md#pointblank.Validate.interrogate). The report shows every step: how many rows passed and failed, which thresholds were reached, and a CSV of the failing rows. With `brief=True`, each step also says in plain words what it checks.

``` python
(
    pb.Validate(
        data=small_table,
        tbl_name="small_table",
        label="Checks on the sales data",
        brief=True,
        thresholds=pb.Thresholds(warning=0.05, error=0.10, critical=0.15),
    )
    .col_vals_gt(columns="d", value=1000)
    .col_vals_not_null(columns="c")
    .col_vals_regex(columns="b", pattern=r"^\d-[a-z]{3}-\d{3}$")
    .col_vals_in_set(columns="f", set=["low", "mid", "high"])
    .rows_distinct()
    .interrogate()
)
```

### See exactly what failed

A failing step is a starting point, not a dead end. Open any step in a report of its own, pull out the rows that failed, or split the table into its passing and failing rows.

A step's own report

The rows where `c` is missing, with the failing values highlighted.

``` python
validation.get_step_report(i=2)
```

### Runs where your data lives

Pointblank works through [Narwhals](https://narwhals-dev.github.io/narwhals/) and [Ibis](https://ibis-project.org), so the same plan runs unchanged on DataFrames and in databases, and the checks happen where the data is.

Polars Pandas PyArrow DuckDB PySpark Snowflake BigQuery Databricks PostgreSQL MySQL SQL Server SQLite CSV and Parquet

[Installation](./user-guide/getting-started/installation.md)

### And when you need more

Validation is the core, and everything else builds on it.

##### Contracts and pipelines

Reusable data contracts, checked where data comes in and where it goes out. Import JSON Schema and Frictionless.

[Data contracts →](./user-guide/contracts-and-pipelines/contracts.md)

##### YAML and the CLI

Keep plans in YAML for review, and run them with `pb` in CI, with exit codes and extracts.

[YAML workflows →](./user-guide/yaml/yaml-validation-workflows.md)

##### Plans drafted by AI

Get a first plan from a model that looked at your table, then revise it in plain English.

[Drafting plans →](./user-guide/advanced-validation/draft-validation.md)

##### Comparing tables

Find the rows and values that differ between two tables, even across backends and large files.

[Comparing tables →](./user-guide/table-comparison/comparing-tables.md)

##### Data for machine learning

Check training splits, synthetic data, and text, then measure which failing rows hurt a model.

[Data ablation →](./user-guide/post-interrogation/data-ablation.md)

##### Look before you validate

Previews, column summaries, and missing-value maps to see what a table holds.

[Data inspection →](./user-guide/data-inspection/preview.md)

##### Test data

Generate realistic data from a schema, in 100+ locales, as a pytest fixture.

[Generating test data →](./user-guide/test-data-generation/generating-test-data.md)

##### Clinical and metadata standards

CDISC SDTM and ADaM, Define-XML, and metadata from SPSS, SAS, and Stata files.

[Metadata import →](./user-guide/metadata-import/metadata-import.md)

##### Agents and observability

An MCP server and Agent Skills for AI assistants, and OpenTelemetry traces and metrics.

[MCP quick start →](./user-guide/integrations/mcp-quick-start.md)

### Get started

Install Pointblank from PyPI:

``` bash
pip install pointblank
```

Then make your first validation in the [Quickstart](./user-guide/getting-started/quickstart.md), or look through the [Demos](./examples/) for ideas. Reports come in [40 languages](./user-guide/post-interrogation/validation-reports.md#reports-in-other-languages).
